videos.script: Every name in a Swift program answers one question. From where may this be used? {{levels}} There are six answers, each a region inside the next. Private, the type. Fileprivate, the file. Internal, the module, which is what you get by writing nothing. {{modules}} Then the planner splits in two. A library with the types, and a program that imports it. And the week the library declared simply vanishes from the program, because nobody marked it public. {{set}} Then a property anyone may read and only its own type may change. {{open}} Then classes. Public lets another module use one. Open lets it subclass one, and the two are separate promises. {{package}} Then the level in between, for code shared by the modules of one package and nobody else. {{names}} And namespaces. Swift has no keyword for them, and does not need one. A module is one, and an enum with no cases is the other. By the end, the planner's library publishes only what it means to.
